newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austrian shares knocked down by profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Austrian shares knocked down by profit-taking.

text.p: Austrian shares followed the international lead and closed 0.77 percent down on Thursday as profit-taking robbed the Vienna market of most of the previous day's gains.
The blue-chip ATX index slipped 8.34 points to 1,072.87 but traders said the underlying tone remained positive.
"The international environment wasn't particularly inspiring and that may have triggered some of the profit-taking," said a trader.
"But I see this as a consolidation at a fairly high level."
Market participants forecast the ATX index would move in a 1,070-1,080 points range in the short term.
Four ATX issues closed higher, 16 lower and one unchanged.
Industrial group OMV and Creditanstalt bank ordinary shares came under selling pressure towards the end of the session, brokers said.

Vienna airport company Flughafen Wien was the day's biggest percentage gainer, rising 0.35 percent, or two schillings, to 572 schillings. Earlier the firm said a cut in its 1996 dividend payment was unlikely.
ATX heavyweight EA-Generali was the biggest percentage decliner. The insurer shed 2.21 percent, or 70 schillings, to close at 3,100 schillings.
Creditanstalt ordinary shares ended 8.9 schillings down at 685.1 while OMV dropped 19.5 schillings to 1,072.
October ATX futures stood four schillings down at 1,075. The broad-based Vienna bourse index eased 3.02 points to 411.74. -- Vienna Newsroom, 43-1-53112-258
